title: Anantapur School Attack: Injured Class 10 Girl Stable After Bleeding Controlled
excerpt: Doctors at Manipal Hospital in Bengaluru have stabilised the student airlifted after Saturday's saw attack at her Rapthadu school, Education Minister Nara Lokesh said, as 20 counsellors were sent to support her classmates.
body:
• The Class 10 student attacked with a saw at Zilla Parishad High School in Rapthadu, Anantapur district, on Saturday is stable after doctors at Manipal Hospital, Bengaluru, controlled her major bleeding, Education Minister Nara Lokesh said.
  • Lokesh said the hospital team stabilised her with blood transfusions and supportive treatment, and that she is undergoing orthopaedic surgery, to be followed by plastic surgery for facial and other injuries.
  • The accused, identified by police as a relative of the student, was arrested at Dharmavaram railway station shortly after the attack, ANI reported.
  • A team of 20 mental health counsellors will make door-to-door visits to all 32 students of Class X-A and to girl students in Classes 8, 9 and 10.

The condition of the Class 10 student attacked inside her school in Andhra Pradesh's Anantapur district has stabilised, Education Minister Nara Lokesh said on Sunday, a day after the assault left her critically injured. Doctors at Manipal Hospital in Bengaluru controlled the major bleeding in the operating theatre and her blood pressure was being maintained, The Hindu reported, citing Lokesh's update on X.

"I am relieved to hear that the doctors have managed to control the bleeding and that her condition is currently stable. She is undergoing orthopaedic surgery, which will be followed by plastic surgery to treat her facial and other injuries."

— Nara Lokesh, Andhra Pradesh Education Minister, on X

From Rapthadu to Bengaluru

On Saturday morning, an intruder entered a Class 10 classroom at Zilla Parishad High School in Rapthadu during school hours and attacked the student with a wood-cutting saw, injuring a classmate who tried to intervene, according to ANI. Lokesh coordinated the emergency response and a green channel to airlift the critically injured girl to Manipal Hospital in Bengaluru. The Hindu reported that the hospital team stabilised her with blood transfusions and supportive treatment, and that Lokesh was likely to reach Bengaluru on Sunday to consult the medical team.

"The child continues to receive close medical attention. We remain hopeful for a full recovery," Lokesh said in the update reported by The Hindu.

Arrest and official response

Anantapur Deputy Superintendent of Police Ashwin Manideep Kakumanu confirmed the attack, saying the accused allegedly attacked the student with a saw inside the school classroom. The accused — identified by police as a relative of the victim — was arrested at Dharmavaram railway station shortly after the incident, ANI reported. The state government, led by Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu and Lokesh, promised strict legal action against the perpetrator and severe consequences for any negligence on school safety.

Support for the students who saw it

On Sunday, Lokesh announced a trauma-response initiative for the school: a dedicated team of 20 mental health counsellors will conduct door-to-door visits for all 32 students of Class X-A, the victim's class, as well as girl students in Classes 8, 9 and 10, according to ANI's report. "No child should have to live or learn in fear," he said. The attack has put the security of government schools — how an outsider carrying a saw entered an occupied classroom — at the centre of the state's response, alongside the criminal case.
